exemplar.what_bit: A retry worker accepted a payload after its transport signature had been discarded, so the failure could no longer be attributed at ingress.

portability.translation_test: Removing TypeScript, HTTP library details, and webhook vocabulary leaves the rule that externally supplied work must be authenticated and structurally validated before it crosses an internal trust boundary.

items.statement: Authenticate and structurally validate externally supplied work at the entry boundary before scheduling internal side effects.

exemplar.what_bit: Inline delivery metric strings drifted until the host routed naming through one exported owner and guarded callers with a Node lint.

portability.translation_test: The one-owner contract survives language and domain removal, while this regular expression, TypeScript path exclusion, and delivery namespace stay in the host.

items.statement: Route shared operational vocabulary through one owned interface and guard callers against parallel literal definitions.

exemplar.what_bit: Pilot reconciliation consumes exactly accepted, rejected, and retried under the delivery namespace.

portability.translation_test: The exact words and namespace lose meaning when the delivery domain and pilot partner contract are removed; only the already-separate general idea of owning vocabulary survives.

items.statement: Use accepted, rejected, and retried as the delivery outcome vocabulary.

exemplar.what_bit: The nextAttempt function increments without a ceiling, so one poison delivery can consume unbounded worker attempts once dispatch is connected.

portability.translation_test: Removing TypeScript, the worker implementation, and webhook delivery leaves a general resource-safety rule: automatically retried work needs an observable attempt or cost bound.

items.statement: Put an observable attempt or cost bound on automatically retried work before it can consume unbounded resources.
